newsitem.title: USA: Senate votes to confirm Tenet as CIA director.
newsitem.headline: Senate votes to confirm Tenet as CIA director.

text.p: The Senate voted late on Thursday to approve President Bill Clinton's nomination of George Tenet to head the Central Intelligence Agency.
The unanimous voice vote came after the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence earlier on Thursday unanimously approved the nomination of Tenet, currently CIA deputy director.
Sen. John Warner, a Virginia Republican, praised Tenet's professional abilities, his character and his judgement.

Warner, who knew Tenet when he was a senior staff member on the Senate Intelligence Committee, said, "I have confidence in him and I am confident that he will represent our country very well in this important post."

The Justice Department on Wednesday concluded a preliminary investigation of Tenet's failure to disclose certain stock and real estate holdings and saw no need to appoint an independent counsel, paving the way for the Senate vote.
Clinton nominated Tenet after Anthony Lake, the president's former national security adviser, withdrew his nomination for the CIA post in frustration over the confirmation process.
